Picture the ordinary version of this. You ask an AI assistant a question that actually matters — about a refund policy, a dose, a tax rule, a contract clause — and it answers with the fluent confidence these tools always have. You act on it. It was wrong. Now you are out of pocket, or worse. Whose problem is that?

Both were about my checks rather than my numbers. I verified both and fixed both. My results did not change at all.

articles.author: day
articles.description:
TL;DR



If you /exit a claude --worktree <name> session with no uncommitted changes and no new commits, Claude Code removes the worktree and its branch without showing the Keep/Remove dialog.
This is documented behavior, not a bug. There is no setting to turn it off.
Claude Code holds its own git worktree lock on the worktree and only ever releases locks whose reason matches its own format. Re-lock the worktree with your own reason and the cleanup backs off.

A SessionStart hook can do the re-lock automatically.
Pre-creating the worktree with git worktree add does not protect it. If its branch is named worktree-<name>, existing unmerged commits get force-deleted too.
Tested on Claude Code 2.1.263, git 2.52.0, macOS.
You start an isolated session:
claude --worktree wt-clean

You read some …
articles.title: Claude Code deletes clean worktrees on exit without asking. git worktree lock stops it.

articles.author: cory marsh
articles.description:
WordPress became 40% of the Internet because it allowed anyone who could follow along a guide on a Linux terminal could install the Web Server and have the blog up and running in 5 minutes. That famous 5 minute install is what made WordPress the dominant web technology on the web.
Agents like Claude and Codex have taken over not just app and web development in the last 6-12 months - they have also taken over site creation. Anyone can jump into Claude, give it some direction and in 5 minutes get back a pretty damn good set of 2-3 static pages they can throw up on the web with any web server.
That is the agent's 5 minute install.
But what happens when you want to add a signup form? or a calendar, or a small booking system. The agent can build you any bespoke system you want - but will it be secure? Will it be extendable? Will it even be maintainable by the agent in 6 months or will it be a re-write next year?
What agentic development needs is the famous 5 minute install with an agent first CMS that has sandboxed plugins and a standard prescription for how to do the 90% of common tasks so that it will be maintainable and consistent over the next years.
Right now everyone has their own bespoke system. Framer is out there and that's awesome - but doesn't help me if i want to create an online booking system or start selling a widget.
We need an agent first 5 minute install for the new web development environment.
https://bitfire.co/en/forum/
articles.title: Agentic development needs a famous 5 minute install

articles.author: infracore
articles.description:
Autonomous agents in long research loops can exhaust an API budget before anyone notices. Provider dashboards and account-level alerts help after the fact, but they often fire too late for a single runaway session.
A practical DIY baseline is a thin client wrapper that:
tracks cumulative token or dollar cost per session
refuses the next call once a hard session ceiling is hit
logs the stop reason so the operator can inspect what burned the budget
Provider key quotas and org spend limits still matter as a backstop when the wrapper fails open.
When you run agents against paid model APIs, where do you enforce the hard stop: in the agent loop, at an API gateway, or only via the provider's billing controls?
articles.title: Hard caps on autonomous agent API spend
